verdict.rationale: Oneleet ships its own public API: an OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec with 157 paths, a separate Auditor API, service keys, and an official MCP server through which an OAuth-connected assistant can do whatever the user's role allows. That is real programmatic coverage. However, nothing documents parity with the UI, and the spec itself says the routes behind the web application are not part of the public API and reject service keys and OAuth tokens. missing for 10: an explicit statement or mapping of API/UI feature parity, evidence that UI-only actions (e.g., MDM remote actions, policy publishing, Trust Center setup) are exposed via the API, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Oneleet serves a downloadable OpenAPI 3.0.3 document for its Public API (157 paths) at the API origin
Use service keys for AI agent automation, MCP servers, and scripts to interact with your Oneleet workspace.
Once connected, the assistant acts as you. It can only see and do what your own role in the workspace allows
